messages.content: my uncle wants to visit tomorrow morning. i want to see him, but i work in the morning. help me answer.
i would like to see you tomorrow. i work in the morning, so could you come in the afternoon instead?
that sounds good. should i explain all my work to him?
you do not need to explain every part of your work. saying that you work in the morning gives him a clear reason for the change.
what if he can only come in the morning?
you could ask about another day. for example: if the afternoon does not work for you, could we choose another day? i want to have time to talk with you.
i do have ten minutes before work. should i say he can come then?
only if you want a short visit and can be clear about the time. you could say: you can come before work, but i can only talk for ten minutes. would another day be better for you?
i would rather have a longer visit. write the whole message without the ten minutes.
i would like to see you tomorrow. i work in the morning, so could you come in the afternoon instead? if that does not work for you, we can choose another day when we have more time to talk.
he said the afternoon is fine. what do i say now?
good, i will see you tomorrow afternoon. what time would you like to come?
write a story about a page that someone cannot find. the page should still be in the house. make the reason simple.

a child wrote a story on a page and put it inside a book. later, she wanted to read the story to her father, but she could not find the page. she looked on her desk and under her chair. then her brother came into the room with another book. he opened it and found the page inside. the child had put her story in his book because the two books looked almost the same. she said thank you and read the story to their father.
why did she look under her chair?
she was trying to find the page and thought it might be on the floor. the story does not say that she knew where it was.
did her brother take the page?
the story does not say that he took it. it says that the child put the page in his book herself.
make the child ask him a question before he opens the book.
she could ask: is that my book or yours? then he could open it and say: it is mine, but this page looks like your story.
why is that a useful question in the story?
it helps them look at the two books and think about which one they each have. his answer also helps them understand that the story page is hers, although the book is his.
can the last part show her doing something to help her find the page next time?

yes. after reading her story, she writes her name at the top of the page and puts it on her own desk. her name helps other people know whose page it is. she also has a place where she can look for it.
if i say i have not finished my book yet, am i saying that i will never finish it?
no. you are saying that you have not finished it up to now. yet often leaves open the idea that you may finish it later. it does not say for sure what will happen.
what about i will not finish this book?
that sentence is about what you think will happen or what you plan to do after now. it is different from saying that the book is not finished at this moment.
i want to tell a friend i am still reading. which one should i use?
you could say: i have not finished the book yet. i am still reading it.
can i say i did not finish the book yesterday?
yes. that gives your friend information about yesterday. it does not say whether you finished the book today or whether you are still reading it.
so if i finished it this morning, what would the whole answer be?
i did not finish the book yesterday, but i finished it this morning.
what if i stopped reading because i did not enjoy it?
you could say: i stopped reading the book because i did not enjoy it. that gives your friend the reason you stopped, without saying that everyone would feel the same way about the book.
please give me just the sentence for still reading.
i have not finished the book yet. i am still reading it.
write a story where two people think they have different food, but they are looking at the same container.

a mother put some rice in a container and left it on the table. her son saw it and said that he had found his lunch. her daughter came in later and said that she had found her dinner. when they talked, they found that both were talking about the same rice. neither had asked their mother who it was for. they went to her together. she said that the rice was for the family meal, and that there was more food in the kitchen.
did either child tell a lie?
the story does not say that either child knew the rice was for the family. they each made an idea about it before asking. being wrong is not always the same as telling a lie.
what should they have asked first?
they could have asked: who is this rice for? that question does not start by saying that the food is already theirs.
why does asking about the container not answer the food question?
knowing whose container it is does not always tell you who may eat the food inside it. someone can use their own container to hold food for other people.
make the mother answer in a kind way.
she could say: that rice is for all of us. i understand why you asked. come into the kitchen and i will show you what else we have for our meal.
what is one thing the children learned?
they learned to ask who food is for before saying that it is their own.
i enjoy talking to my friend, but after work i sometimes want to sit alone. how do i say that without making it sound like i hate our conversations?
you could say: i enjoy talking with you. after work, i sometimes need a quiet break before i am ready to talk. can we talk a little later?
i do not know when i will be ready. should i still give a time?
you do not have to give a time that you do not know you can keep. you could ask to send a message when you are ready, or choose another day that would work for both of you.
please write the message with sending something later.
i enjoy talking with you, but i need some quiet time after work today. may i send you a message later when i am ready to talk?
what if my friend asks whether they did something wrong?
you can answer that question clearly if you know the answer. for example: you did not do anything wrong. i am tired after work and need a little time alone.
that is true for me. make it less long.
you did not do anything wrong. i am tired and need a quiet break. i will send you a message later.
would my need for a break mean that i am not a good friend?
no. your need for time alone does not by itself tell us whether you are a good friend. being clear and kind can help your friend understand what you need, while leaving room for their feelings too.
i need to wash a cup before i use it for tea. i also want to read a page. must i read before washing the cup?
no. from what you said, washing the cup must come before using it for tea. you did not give a rule about when to read the page.
can i wash the cup, read the page, and then make tea?
yes. in that order, the cup is washed before you use it. reading the page between those things does not break your rule.
what about making tea and washing the cup after?
that would not follow your rule if you use the cup before washing it. you said the cup needs to be washed first.
if i read first and then wash the cup, is the whole plan wrong?
no. you can read first, then wash the cup, then use it for tea. the important order is between washing the cup and using it, not between reading and washing.
explain why the first thing in my message does not have to be the first thing i do.

a message can list things without giving a full order for them. words such as before and after tell us which parts must come first. in your message, before makes it clear that you must wash the cup before using it for tea.
give me one possible plan in one sentence.
read the page, wash the cup, and then use the clean cup for tea.
write a story about a person who tries to help before understanding what help is needed.

a boy saw his grandmother looking at a page for a long time. he thought she could not read the small words, so he began reading them to her. she said thank you, but told him that she could read the words herself. she was trying to remember where she had seen the same story before. the boy stopped reading and asked what she remembered about it. together, they talked about the old book she used to keep near her bed. then she remembered where to look.
was reading to her always the wrong thing to do?
no. reading to someone can be useful when they want that help. here, the boy had not asked what she needed, so his first idea did not answer her real question.
what could he ask before starting?
he could ask: would you like me to read that page, or are you thinking about something else?
why is the other choice useful?
it leaves room for her to explain what she is doing. she does not have to choose between getting help she does not need and saying that she wants no help at all.
can you make the last part about her finding the old book?
yes. after their conversation, she looked on the shelf in her bedroom. the old book was there. she opened it and found the story she remembered. this time, she asked the boy to read it with her.
what changed about the help at the end?
she asked for it, and they both understood what they were going to do together.
is do you know where the library is a question about whether someone knows, or about the place?
it can do both in conversation. the words ask whether the person knows the place, but people often use that question when they want the person to tell them where it is.
if someone answers only yes, is that false?
not if they really know. yes can answer the words of the question, but it may not give the information the other person was asking for.
how can i ask more clearly?
you can say: please tell me where the library is. or you can ask: where is the library?
why is it where the library is in one sentence and where is the library in the other?
where is the library is a question by itself. in please tell me where the library is, the part after tell me sits inside a larger request. in that part, the library comes before is.
give me a similar pair about a book.
where is my book? please tell me where my book is.
what if the other person does not know?
they can say: i do not know where your book is. that is more clear than making up a place just to give an answer.
can they still help?
yes. they might ask where you last used it, or help you look. not knowing the answer at first does not mean that they cannot help at all.
